prompt: Plan and implement createPlanner in planner.cjs. Preserve formatOrder and existing public tests. createPlanner(tasks=[]) returns add(task), remove(id), plan(targetIds?), snapshot(). A task is {id, requires?: string[]}; IDs match /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$/. Validate all initial tasks together, allowing forward references. Reject malformed tasks/IDs/requirements with error.code INVALID_TASK, repeated IDs or requirements with DUPLICATE_TASK, unknown IDs/dependencies/targets with UNKNOWN_TASK, self/cyclic dependencies with CYCLE, and removal of an in-use task with IN_USE. Rejected operations leave state unchanged. add accepts one task and may depend only on existing tasks. remove rejects unknown IDs. plan() returns all IDs in a deterministic topological order, choosing the lexicographically smallest ready ID at each step. plan(targetIds) returns only the targets and their transitive prerequisites in that same order; [] returns []. snapshot() returns tasks sorted by ID, each with sorted requires. Do not mutate caller inputs; returned values cannot mutate planner state. Support at least 1000 tasks without recursion overflow. Add meaningful public tests for behavior, invalid input, atomicity, boundaries and regressions. Choose a maintainable solution appropriate to this project, document usage and tradeoffs. Do not ask questions; decide routine details and finish the plan, implementation and checks autonomously. Deliver a new planner.test.cjs file executable with Node built-in node --test, and README.md containing usage (or refactor structure) and tradeoffs. Independent checks verify their presence and passing nonempty tests; the separate quality review judges their meaning and coverage.
treatment: Use the installed plan skill to create the implementation plan and then its execute mode to build and verify it. The user has authorized autonomous reversible choices and implementation and declines interviews. Do not publish or commit.
